operation.summary: Zoom in on something in a photo: crop to what query finds (or to a box you give) with some margin. which=first (default), all (one crop around every match) or each (one crop per match, 10 at most)

body.name: capture_id
body.description: A photo this agent captured and kept (POST /v1/camera/snapshot with store), or one shared with it

body.name: gallery_id
body.description: An accessible gallery photo (also needs the gallery grant)

body.name: data_base64
body.description: The image bytes instead (JPEG, PNG or WebP; about 1.5 MB of image at most, so use capture_id or gallery_id for big photos)

body.name: query
body.description: What to crop to; or give box instead

body.name: box
body.description: {x0, y0, x1, y1} fractions (0-1) of the upright photo, for example from /v1/images/find

body.name: index
body.description: With which=first: the match to use, 0 = most prominent

body.name: pad
body.description: Margin around the box as a fraction of its size on each side, 0-2, default 0.15

body.name: aspect
body.description: Optional width/height of the crop, for example 1 for square

body.name: mode
body.description: auto (default: faces on the phone, everything else in the cloud), on_device (faces only, never uploads) or cloud

body.name: engine
body.description: Opt-in: on_device_detector finds anything named in words on the phone (free, offline, 7-16 s; GET /v1/images/engines). Never falls back to the cloud; model_not_ready while its model downloads. Other detector engines may appear in GET /v1/images/engines

body.name: outline
body.description: Opt-in: also trace each item's outline on the phone (on_device_outline engine, +3-4 s): items get outline [[x, y], ...] fractions. On crop, each crop is a PNG cut out along the outline (transparent outside)

body.name: max_edge_px
body.description: Longest side of each crop, 64-4096, default 2048

body.name: raw
body.description: 1 = return the JPEG bytes (which=first or all only)

operation.returns: JPEG (PNG cut-out with outline) (data_base64, width_px, height_px) with crop {left,top,right,bottom px} and the found items; which=each: crops [...]
